Hi Vivek,

We're preparing the internal case to move from the current reserved tier to the Enterprise Upgrade (multi-region, higher throughput). Our CFO needs clear, short evidence showing the outcomes and unit economics your platform enabled over the last 6 months. Specifically: average latency improvements for our peak workloads, measured cost-per-1M tokens (before/after implementing caching), and 2–3 quantifiable customer-facing outcomes we can quote in the internal deck.

Can you send a short "evidence packet" we can share with finance today? A CSV with usage/latency and a one-pager with suggested bullets/quotes would be ideal. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Mark Cullen
Account Executive
Brighthouse Analytics

Hi all — attached is the raw export (Brighthouse_usage_report_Q1.csv). Highlights I recommend we call out on the one-pager:

- Peak 95th latency improved from 420ms -> 180ms after prefix caching and switching to the dedicated q8 model variant (38% latency at-scale).
- Average cost per 1M tokens reduced from $18.70 -> $11.40 after batching + KV caching — a ~39% unit cost reduction.
- Observed throughput: steady-state 2.4k reqs/min across a 6-hour peak window; Enterprise upgrade projection (reserved GPUs) would increase sustainable throughput by ~3.8x.

I also pulled three anonymized customer-facing outcomes we can use as bullets (short, quantified):
- Reduced user query abandonment by ~14% during peak hours after latency improvements.
- 21% increase in completions that matched the quality threshold in A/B tests after applying our model routing policy.
- Estimated monthly infrastructure savings of ~$12.6k (projected) when moving to a dedicated capacity plan at current run rate.

I'll attach the CSV now and a quick sample chart export.

Attachment: Brighthouse_usage_report_Q1.csv

- Dylan
Senior Data Analyst, Redwood Inference
